newsitem.title: UK: UK cereal yields seen good, quality lower - Dalgety.
newsitem.headline: UK cereal yields seen good, quality lower - Dalgety.

text.p: UK cereal harvest results are showing good yield but some quality reduction, according to preliminary estimates from UK firm Dalgety Agriculture's nationwide farm survey.
The company said it has sampled and analysed more than one million tonnes of wheat and barley harvested before recent rains.

"Initial wheat results suggest moisture is up to 1.5 percent higher than last year, and Class 1 and 2 wheat proteins are 0.3 percent lower," Dalgety's director of purchasing and trading, Andrew Barnard, said in a statement.
"Feed wheat proteins are very similar to last year," he said.
But he said it was too early to make a confident prediction on yield and quality since about 60 percent of the wheat harvest has still to be gathered in north England and Scotland.
Barnard said initial results showed that screenings were about two percent lower than last year for all classes of wheat.
"Low screenings coupled with high bushel weight suggest that the grains are very bold and heavy, resulting in a high thousand grain weight and thus high yield," he said.
The barley crop suffered considerable stress at the growth stage from the long dry spell during May and June.
This lead to high screenings and high nitrogen but fortunately the yield appears to have held. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
